questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a genuine high-availability design in Cosmos DB require?
options: Combining the right choices in distribution, consistency, and conflict resolution together, matched to the specific workload
Enabling Strong consistency everywhere regardless of workload
Choosing only the cheapest throughput model available
A single setting that automatically configures everything correctly
questions.explain: The lesson's core argument is that HA is a combination of deliberate, interacting choices, not one setting or the strongest option in each category.

questions.q: According to this lesson's guidance on consistency, what should a team choose for a workload like a social media timeline?
options: The weakest consistency level the workload can honestly tolerate, such as Session or Eventual, rather than the strongest available
Always Strong consistency, since correctness is always the top priority
No consistency level needs to be set for read-heavy workloads
Bounded Staleness is mandatory for all workloads regardless of need
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly argues for matching consistency to actual need — over-choosing Strong costs latency/availability for a guarantee the workload doesn't require.

questions.q: Why is Last-Writer-Wins a poor fit for a shopping cart container, per this lesson?
options: Silently dropping a customer's cart item on conflict is a real incident, unlike telemetry data where losing the 'losing' write doesn't matter
LWW is technically incompatible with shopping cart data structures
LWW can only be used with the MongoDB API
Shopping carts cannot be stored in a multi-region-write container at all
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes data where losing a write silently is acceptable (telemetry) from data where it's a real problem (a customer's cart), which needs custom conflict resolution instead.

questions.q: What happens if a team enables multi-region writes without a deliberate conflict resolution strategy, per this lesson?
options: They risk silent data loss from unresolved or poorly-resolved conflicts
Multi-region writes automatically disable themselves until a strategy is set
Nothing — conflict resolution is irrelevant unless Strong consistency is also enabled
The account reverts automatically to single-region write mode
questions.explain: The lesson warns this exact scenario exposes the application to silent data loss, since conflicts become possible the moment multiple regions can write.

questions.q: Why does choosing Strong consistency across distant regions undermine multi-region writes, per this lesson?
options: It undermines the latency benefit multi-region writes was meant to provide
Strong consistency is not supported at all in multi-region-write accounts
It has no real effect on latency, only on cost
It automatically disables the change feed
questions.explain: Strong consistency requires cross-region confirmation, which works against the low-latency goal that motivated enabling multi-region writes in the first place.
